name: Bodh Gaya
summary: The holiest place in Buddhism: the Buddha attained enlightenment here under the Bodhi tree, and the Mahabodhi Temple now stands beside a descendant of that tree. Monasteries built by Buddhist nations from Bhutan to Japan ring the town, and the ruins of Nalanda university and the hills of Rajgir make a full-day trip.
seasonNote: October to March is cool and dry; December and January bring Tibetan pilgrims, prayer festivals and sometimes teachings by the Dalai Lama. April to June is very hot.
arrival: Gaya airport (15 minutes away) has flights from Delhi and Kolkata and seasonal flights from Southeast Asia. Gaya Junction station is 30 minutes away, with trains from Delhi, Varanasi and Kolkata.
gettingAround: The town is small and walkable; e-rickshaws link the temples and monasteries. Hire a car for Nalanda and Rajgir.
cashTip: Carry cash; cards work only in bigger hotels. UPI is common.
foodTip: Monastery guesthouses and Tibetan cafés serve thukpa and momos; try Bihar's litti chokha, roasted wheat balls with mashed aubergine.
buyTip: Prayer beads, singing bowls, Buddha statues and Tibetan textiles from the market by the temple.
baseArea: Hotels and monastery guesthouses within walking distance of the Mahabodhi Temple

connections.note: Train from Gaya Junction; about 6 hours by road.

items.name: Mahabodhi Temple and the Bodhi Tree
items.summary: The 50 m brick temple marking the spot of the Buddha's enlightenment, with the sacred Bodhi tree and the Vajrasana diamond throne behind it.
items.expect: Shoes off at the gate; phones are not allowed inside (use the lockers); open to all.
items.tip: Come at dawn or dusk to sit among monks chanting under the tree.

items.name: Dungeshwari Cave Temples
items.summary: Cave shrines where the Buddha is said to have fasted for six years before going to Bodh Gaya.
items.expect: A short climb; small Tibetan monastery at the top.
items.tip: Go in the morning with a rickshaw; children may beg, so give to the monastery instead.

items.expect: A large site with a museum; little shade.
